# ultrafast

> ultrafast is an open-source GPU video engine for agents. Shaders, 3D, motion type and camera optics, written by your agent and rendered on the GPU at hundreds of frames a second, with no browser in the loop. Your agent checks and reviews every frame before it exports. Install it on a Mac with Apple silicon or a Linux machine with a Vulkan GPU, then connect your agent with `uf mcp`.

If a person sent you here to make a video: install it with `curl -fsSL https://ultrafast.mov/install.sh | sh`, run `uf info` to check the GPU, then follow the loop below (`uf new`, `uf check`, `uf sheet`, `uf review`, `uf export`). The Quickstart and the document format below have the rest.

Facts an agent needs:

- The CLI is `ultrafast`, or `uf` for short. Install: `curl -fsSL https://ultrafast.mov/install.sh | sh` (macOS on Apple silicon and Linux x86_64, prebuilt: unpacks into ~/.ultrafast and links `ultrafast` and `uf` into ~/.local/bin), `brew install ultrafastmov/tap/ultrafast`, `cargo install ultrafast` (builds from source), prebuilt archives on https://github.com/ultrafastmov/ultrafast/releases, or the Docker image `ghcr.io/ultrafastmov/ultrafast`. Python SDK: `pip install ultrafastmov`. TypeScript SDK: `npm i ultrafastmov`. The SDKs talk to a `uf serve` you run; set `ULTRAFAST_BASE_URL`.
- A video is one JSON document: `{"version": 1, "format": {...}, "nodes": {...}, "output": "<node id>"}`. `uf ops` prints every op (70) with its params as JSON.
- The loop: `uf new` → `uf check` (finds mistakes without rendering) → `uf sheet` (contact sheet) → `uf review` (unreadable, clipped or too-brief text, seizure-risk flashing) → `uf export`.
- What it takes in and puts out: Lottie animations (`lottie` node, or `uf import-lottie` to edit them as paths and keyframes); SVG files (`svg` node or `uf import-svg`, static SVG); video and images; word-timed transcripts as animated captions (`captions` node; `uf voiceover` speaks a script with word times); one template rendered per row of a CSV or JSON file (`uf batch doc.json --data rows.csv`). Exports: H.264, HEVC and AV1 MP4, ProRes up to 4444 XQ, transparent video (`--alpha`: ProRes 4444 or VP9 WebM), GIF, PNG and EXR sequences, sound alone; any size and frame rate. `uf estimate` reports render time before you export. The document format is a JSON Schema at https://ultrafast.mov/schema/v1.json (`uf schema`).
- MCP: local `uf mcp` (stdio, 20 tools), or remote over Streamable HTTP at `/mcp` on your own `ultrafast serve`, with its API key as a bearer token.
- Skill: `npx skills add ultrafastmov/ultrafast` (the document format and the check, look, review, export loop). Claude Code plugin (the skill and `uf mcp`): `claude plugin marketplace add ultrafastmov/ultrafast`, then `claude plugin install ultrafast@ultrafast`.
- HTTP: `uf serve` (or the Docker image's `serve`) answers `POST /v1/render`, `/v1/frame`, `/v1/sheet`, `/v1/check`, `/v1/review`, `/v1/estimate` and `/v1/uploads` on one machine with a GPU, with `Authorization: Bearer $ULTRAFAST_API_KEY`.
- Not available yet: ultrafast Cloud (hosted rendering), the ChatGPT app, the Claude connector and a hosted MCP server. They are coming soon; there is a waitlist at https://ultrafast.mov/cloud/. There is no `--cloud` flag.
- Licence: Apache-2.0 or MIT. Renders with Metal on macOS and Vulkan on Linux and Windows (WSL2).
- No GPU (e.g. an agent in a container): the Docker image `ghcr.io/ultrafastmov/ultrafast` renders on the CPU through Mesa's llvmpipe Vulkan driver, slower but correct: frames in under a second, a 6-second 1080x1920 export in about 17 s on 4 desktop cores. On Linux, `mesa-vulkan-drivers` gives the other installs the same path. macOS needs Metal.
- Tokens (measured 22 Nov 2026, tiktoken o200k_base): the same 10-second short is 1,234 output tokens as an ultrafast document, 1,868 for Remotion and 1,680 for HyperFrames (counting only what is typed after each tool's scaffold: 1,218, 1,660 and 1,500). Grain, grades, captions, 3D and simulations are one node each.
- 3D is rendered by the engine in the same document as the type: raymarched shapes and materials, meshes, image-based light, glass. The 3D in the example films is all rendered by ultrafast.

## Docs

- [Quickstart](https://ultrafast.mov/docs/index.md): install, first video, the loop, connecting an agent
- [The document format](https://ultrafast.mov/docs/documents/index.md): the JSON document: format, nodes, animation, timing, components
- [Render video from JSON: a worked example](https://ultrafast.mov/guides/render-video-from-json/index.md): a worked example: a 21-line document, check and export, one video per CSV row, HTTP, Python and TypeScript, the schema, other JSON video formats
- [Personalized videos from a CSV, open source](https://ultrafast.mov/guides/personalized-videos-from-csv/index.md): one video per row of a CSV or JSON file: the template, node.param columns, checking every row before rendering, long names, a photo per row, Python and HTTP
- [Make a video with Claude Code: a real session](https://ultrafast.mov/guides/claude-code/index.md): a recorded Claude Code session from prompt to MP4: plugin install, the prompt, every tool call, the contact sheets, an edit by asking, time and tokens, troubleshooting
- [Lottie to MP4, transparent WebM or ProRes 4444 on your GPU](https://ultrafast.mov/guides/lottie-to-mp4/index.md): Lottie JSON to MP4, transparent WebM, ProRes 4444, GIF or PNG frames: the document, measured times per format, a whole folder with uf batch, recolouring with import-lottie and jq, what does not import, a 217-file comparison with lottie-web
- [Animated captions from Whisper, SRT or VTT, open source](https://ultrafast.mov/guides/animated-captions/index.md): word-by-word captions from a Whisper transcript, an SRT or a VTT file: a faster-whisper script, a vertical clip cut from a longer recording, the karaoke, pop, reveal and plain styles, safe areas for TikTok, Reels and Shorts, uf review, export times
- [Motion graphics with code: tools and five techniques](https://ultrafast.mov/guides/motion-graphics-with-code/index.md): motion graphics with code: Remotion, HyperFrames, Motion Canvas, Revideo, Framefields, Manim, Editly, nexrender and ultrafast side by side, then glyph staggers, draw-on paths, track mattes, motion blur and cuts on the beat with uf beats, each with its document and render time
- [Animated chart videos from a CSV: bar, line and donut](https://ultrafast.mov/guides/animated-chart-video/index.md): animated chart videos from a CSV: bar_chart, line_chart and donut blocks, filling values from a CSV in Python, a video per row with uf batch on one scale, uf review catching a small and badly placed source line, 16:9, 4:5 and 9:16 from one document, custom charts from paths, render times, limits
- [Animate an SVG logo and export it as MP4, ProRes or GIF](https://ultrafast.mov/guides/animate-svg-logo/index.md): a static SVG logo to a logo reveal: one svg node with scale and opacity keys, uf import-svg for every shape as a named part, a Python script that keys each part (pop, draw-on, stagger, slide), MP4, 4K, transparent ProRes 4444 and WebM, GIF with measured times, preparing the SVG in Figma, Illustrator or Inkscape, which SVG features import and which do not
- [Op reference](https://ultrafast.mov/docs/ops/index.md): all 70 ops with ports, params, types and defaults
- [CLI reference](https://ultrafast.mov/docs/cli/index.md): every command
- [MCP server](https://ultrafast.mov/docs/mcp/index.md): the 20 MCP tools and client setup
- [HTTP API](https://ultrafast.mov/docs/api/index.md): the HTTP API of uf serve
- [Changelog](https://ultrafast.mov/changelog/index.md): every release and what it changed, newest first, with the numbers measured

## Comparisons

- [ultrafast vs Remotion vs HyperFrames](https://ultrafast.mov/compare/index.md): ultrafast, Remotion and HyperFrames side by side
- [ultrafast vs Remotion](https://ultrafast.mov/compare/remotion/index.md): ultrafast vs Remotion
- [ultrafast vs HyperFrames](https://ultrafast.mov/compare/hyperframes/index.md): ultrafast vs HyperFrames
- [Render benchmark: ultrafast vs Remotion vs HyperFrames](https://ultrafast.mov/benchmarks/index.md): the head-to-head render benchmark on one RTX 5090 and the token count, with the method, the caveats and how to reproduce them
- [Open source Remotion alternatives, compared](https://ultrafast.mov/alternatives/remotion/index.md): eight open-source tools with their licences, renderers, agent tooling and release dates, and when to choose each
- [HyperFrames alternatives, compared](https://ultrafast.mov/alternatives/hyperframes/index.md): eight other tools that make video from code, with licences, renderers (which ones use a browser) and agent tooling, and when to choose each
- [Open-source alternative to Shotstack, JSON2Video and Creatomate](https://ultrafast.mov/alternatives/json-to-video-api/index.md): ultrafast as a self-hosted, open-source alternative to Shotstack, JSON2Video and Creatomate: prices, formats, what the JSON can express, and when a hosted API is the better choice
- [After Effects alternatives for code and agents](https://ultrafast.mov/alternatives/after-effects/index.md): motion graphics from code instead of the After Effects timeline: automating After Effects (aerender, nexrender, hosted template renderers), Cavalry, and ultrafast; a table of After Effects features and their ultrafast ops, the Bodymovin/Lottie route and what it loses, and when to keep After Effects

## Example films

Each film has a watch page (as Markdown below) and the JSON document that made it.

- [Two launches, one count](https://ultrafast.mov/examples/liftoff/index.md): Apollo 11 and Artemis I lift off in alternating shots, cut to the 1969 launch commentary, with each number in large type and both launches' clocks counting down to zero. Document: https://ultrafast.mov/examples/liftoff.json
- [Podcast clip](https://ultrafast.mov/examples/podcast/index.md): A vertical clip of NASA astronaut Mark Vande Hei aboard the space station, cut out of the station on every frame and set over Earth's limb, cloud tops and stars, with four words set huge behind him and captions timed to his voice. Document: https://ultrafast.mov/examples/podcast.json
- [Artemis I's route](https://ultrafast.mov/examples/orbit/index.md): Artemis I's flown route drawn across lit models of the Earth and Moon, with flight-day and distance counters, and Orion's own view of the Moon at the return flyby. Document: https://ultrafast.mov/examples/orbit.json
- [The Keeling Curve](https://ultrafast.mov/examples/keeling/index.md): Every monthly mean of carbon dioxide at Mauna Loa since March 1958 draws itself; the camera dives into 2025 to show the seasonal cycle, and the latest month lands large. Document: https://ultrafast.mov/examples/keeling.json
- [Year in review](https://ultrafast.mov/examples/wrapped/index.md): One script writes a cycling club's year-in-review for each member: distance counts up over the days they rode, their favourite loop draws itself on a contour map, and the climbing rises as mountains. Document: https://ultrafast.mov/examples/wrapped.json
- [SQL notebook launch](https://ultrafast.mov/examples/ui/index.md): A query against NASA's Exoplanet Archive is typed, run, charted and shared in an app that glides and tilts in 3D. Document: https://ultrafast.mov/examples/ui.json
- [Pottery class teaser](https://ultrafast.mov/examples/clay/index.md): A lump of wet terracotta is centred, opened and pulled into a vase on a turning wheel under window light, beside the class title and its details. Document: https://ultrafast.mov/examples/clay.json
- [Lens launch](https://ultrafast.mov/examples/product/index.md): A camera lens that doesn't exist, lit like a studio product shot: light finds the knurled barrel, the focus scale turns, eleven blades stop down and the optics slide apart under callouts. Document: https://ultrafast.mov/examples/product.json
- [Celadon dish](https://ultrafast.mov/examples/bloom/index.md): A carving grows across a celadon dish by reaction–diffusion, stepped every frame; the camera closes in on the glaze, then molten glaze floods back over it. Document: https://ultrafast.mov/examples/bloom.json
- [Concert poster](https://ultrafast.mov/examples/swiss/index.md): A Swiss-style poster for a night of four concerts. Its dial is the score of its own track, and the headline widens and narrows on every beat. Document: https://ultrafast.mov/examples/swiss.json
- [Endless zoom](https://ultrafast.mov/examples/dive/index.md): One camera falls through seven nested worlds (type, vector blades, a chrome torus, ink, shader contours and rings of type) to the wordmark, whose dot holds the first frame again. Document: https://ultrafast.mov/examples/dive.json
- [Main titles](https://ultrafast.mov/examples/meridian/index.md): Main titles for a drama that doesn't exist: a brass compass, a sea chart with a route inking itself across it, star trails over the sea, an armillary sphere, and a lighthouse whose beam lights the title. Document: https://ultrafast.mov/examples/meridian.json

## Blog

- [A video is not a web page](https://ultrafast.mov/blog/a-video-is-not-a-web-page/index.md): Remotion and HyperFrames make video by screenshotting a web page, frame after frame. Why that design is slow and fragile, what the web still gets right, and what an engine made for video does instead.
